Tom found out that his best golfing friend was having an affair with his wife. Rather than get involved in anything unpleasant like a row, they decided to play eighteen holes - the winner to have complete ownership of the lady.
Ethel was keenly interested in all of Belgrave's activities starting back in the 1930's when she first met Tom and encouraged him in his many successes.
Perhaps he might care to have a go at the course record held by Nick Rose who will be running - as will Mark Rowland, Steve Brace, Tom and Jack Buckner.

Charlie Jones recalled 1930, the year when Tom joined the Club: "Tom Morell and I were down at Battersea track and we saw this slim blonde chap running round and looking really good.

To all Tom's wonderful friends and fellow Belgravians. I would like to express my sincere thanks for the wonderful attendance at Tom's funeral and for the many beautiful letters and cards and flowers.

When Surrey County's magnificent F.N.Pickett Cup was displayed at Committee two days after our Surrey team win, the look on Bill Lucas' face was an absolute treat to behold; and wouldn't old Tom have been delighted.

And of course Sir Eddie Kulukundis was a fixture to his seat throughout the Championships. Clive did manage to chat to Mark Shearman a couple of times and mentioned that we'd like a copy of a photo of Tom for The Belgravian.
